question: What CALABARZON freshwater leads and fish-specific evidence does the Quezon 2025 Ecological Profile page support?
purpose: Record source-named Quezon river leads without converting province-level fisheries context into site-specific fish presence.

sourceDetails.pageTitle: Socio Economic Profile — 2025 Ecological Profile of Quezon Province
sourceDetails.profileDescription: Official page says the 2025 Ecological Profile has six volumes and is a provincial planning/research reference.

links.result: redirected to online form; volume not retrieved
redirected to online form; volume not retrieved

pageFindings.inlandFisheries: The page says inland fisheries occur in major rivers and lakes and lists white goby, freshwater shrimps, catfish, tilapia, mudfish, and mullet as broad freshwater context. It does not assign these names to a river, lake, date, or station. Milkfish and prawns are mentioned as common fishpond culture, not river records.

sourceNamedFeatures.locality: Sariaya; page attributes central river basin designation to DENR

pageFindings.limit: The reviewed page gives no river-specific fish table, collection date, station, voucher, coordinate, channel route, salinity measurement, or geometry.

fishEvidenceDisposition.reason: No waterbody/station crosswalk supports site-specific fish presence.

scopeDecision.reason: Four official page names are preserved as separate research leads; channel routes, identity overlaps, and basin/channel distinctions remain unresolved.

nextActions: Retrieve profile volumes through an authorized download or the province data-request process; no request has been sent.
Seek dated, station-resolved fish surveys with explicit river/reach crosswalks and item-specific reuse terms for all four leads.
Use authoritative hydrography to distinguish the MalakingIlog basin from channel and resolve river routes; do not infer geometry from the page text.
Keep province-wide common-name fisheries context separate unless a source assigns records to a specific waterbody.
nonClaims: No listed fish is asserted as present in Umiray, Agos, Nakar, or MalakingIlog individually.
No fish absence, complete checklist, taxonomic identity, current status, catchability, access, safety, regulation, or diet is inferred.
No channel geometry, watershed polygon, municipal-water boundary, or Agos/JICA system crosswalk is asserted.
